title: Integral closure of an affine torsion-free monoid algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P$ a fine commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], such that $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is torsion free. Put $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{g\in G:ng\in P\text{ for some integer }n>0\}$. For a submonoid $Q\subseteq G$ write $k[Q]=\bigoplus_{q\in Q}ke^q$, with multiplication $e^qe^{q'}=e^{q+q'}$. The natural maps embed $k[P]\subseteq k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]\subseteq k[G]$, all three rings are integral domains, and they have the same fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])$. Inside $K$, $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is the integral closure of $k[P]$: it is exactly the set of elements of $K$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $k[P]$. Moreover $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is a finite $k[P]$-module and is integrally closed in $K$. The zero-rank case $P=G=\{0\}$ and monoids with nontrivial units are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Put $Q=P^{\mathrm{sat}}$. Since $P$ is fine, it is finitely generated and embeds in $G$. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], $Q$ is finitely generated, integral and saturated, its group completion is $G$, and $k[Q]$ is a finite $k[P]$-module. This proves the finiteness clause and supplies the finite-generation hypothesis for $Q$ used next.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-domain-fraction] to $P\subseteq G$ and to $Q\subseteq G$. Both monoids are finitely generated and generate the torsion-free group $G$. The monomial maps embed $k[P]\subseteq k[Q]\subseteq k[G]$, all three are domains, and their fraction fields identify with $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])$. In particular the inclusion is $k[G]\subseteq K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: For each $g\in Q$, the monomial criterion [lem-trf-monomial-integrality] gives that $e^g$ is integral over $k[P]$. The final clause of that node gives that every element of $k[Q]$ is integral over $k[P]$. Thus $k[Q]$ is contained in the integral closure of $k[P]$ inside $K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: The finite generators of $P$ generate $G$ as a group. Since $G$ is torsion free, [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives a finite basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $G$. Put $B_0=k$ and $B_i=B_{i-1}[X_i]$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. The field $k$ is a normal domain: its fraction field is itself. Inductively [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] says that $B_i$ is a normal domain whenever $B_{i-1}$ is one. Hence $B=B_r=k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$ is a normal domain, including $B=k$ when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal, iterated r times; finite-basis input is the existing Mathlib leaf lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free.

proof.text: Let $S=\{X_1^{b_1}\cdots X_r^{b_r}:b_i\in\mathbf N\}\subset B$. Since $B$ is a domain and these monomials are nonzero, $0\notin S$. The map $X_i\mapsto e^{u_i}$ defines $B\to k[G]$; the elements of $S$ map to units, with $(e^{u_i})^{-1}=e^{-u_i}$, so it extends to $\theta:S^{-1}B\to k[G]$. Define its inverse on the monomial basis by $e^{\sum_i n_i u_i}\mapsto\prod_iX_i^{n_i^+}/\prod_iX_i^{n_i^-}$, where $n_i^+=\max(n_i,0)$ and $n_i^-=\max(-n_i,0)$, and extend $k$-linearly. The unique basis coordinates make this well defined; multiplying fractions adds the exponent vectors, so this is a ring map. Both composites fix the coefficients, all $X_i$ and $X_i^{-1}$, respectively every $e^g$, and hence are identities. Thus $k[G]\simeq S^{-1}B$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.12 proof, printed p.104, identification k[P^gp] with k[Z^n]; explicit monomial maps and inverses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] to the normal domain $B$ and the multiplicative subset $S$, which does not contain zero. It gives that $S^{-1}B$ is a normal domain. The explicit isomorphism of the previous step therefore shows that $k[G]$ is integrally closed in its fraction field $K$: every $z\in K$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $k[G]$ lies in $k[G]$. This is the ambient-field assertion needed before discussing support.

source.place: Tag 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain (lines 8048--8062): any localization of a normal domain is normal; Tag 0309, definition-domain-normal.

proof.text: Let $x\in K$ be integral over $k[P]$. A monic equation $x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$ with $a_i\in k[P]$ is also a monic equation over $k[G]$, because $k[P]\subseteq k[G]$. The ambient-field assertion just proved implies $x\in k[G]$. Only now write its finite support $x=\sum_{g\in T}c_ge^g$. By [lem-trf-integral-support-saturation], every $g\in T$ belongs to $Q$. Therefore $x\in k[Q]$. Together with Step 3, this proves that $k[Q]$ is exactly the integral closure of $k[P]$ in $K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Finally let $y\in K$ be integral over $k[Q]$. Its monic equation also has coefficients in $k[G]$, so Step 6 gives $y\in k[G]$. By Step 1, $Q$ is finitely generated and saturated, with torsion-free group completion $G$. Apply [lem-trf-saturated-monoid-algebra-normal] to $Q$ and this element $y$ of $k[G]$: its statement gives $y\in k[Q]$. This proves integral closedness in the full field $K$, rather than only in the group algebra. All arguments allow $r=0$ and negative basis coordinates, so neither the zero-rank case nor monoids with units require an exception.
